title: Compatibility adapter for tool/function call schemas with soft validation and coercion
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: multiple teams and third-party adapters submit tool/function call JSON payloads that use slightly different schema shapes (optional snake_case vs camelCase, numeric strings, enums as free text). Strict validation causes hard rejections and customer-facing errors. Goal: design a compatibility adapter layer and a compact JSON Schema extension that supports lenient validation modes, deterministic coercion rules, and human-friendly error classification so the runtime can accept more inputs without silently changing semantics or losing auditability.
acceptance_criteria: Define a compact schema extension (annotation namespace) that expresses coercion hints, aliasing, and deprecation metadata
Implement three validation modes: strict, lenient, and coerce (runtime flag per-route)
Runtime must emit structured validation diagnostics with stable error codes and suggested fixes
Coercions must be deterministic, reversible for logs (original value recorded), and opt-in per-parameter
Compatibility adapter feature gated behind runtime-1.23 flag and covered by unit + integration tests using representative third-party payloads
notes: Proposal uses an annotation prefix x-redwood-call to avoid colliding with community JSON Schema keywords
Key annotations: x-redwood-call:aliases (list), x-redwood-call:coerce (ruleset id), x-redwood-call:validationMode (strict|lenient|coerce), x-redwood-call:deprecatedSince

Coercion ruleset examples: string->number (parseInt/parseFloat), number->string (toString), enum soft-match (case-insensitive, fuzzy limited to 1 edit), timestamp coercions (ISO fallback to epoch seconds), collection delimited strings -> arrays
We will provide a reference implementation module in the runtime (go) and a JS shim for SDK-local validation to match server behavior

Trade-offs: lenient mode reduces customer friction but increases risk of accidental semantic drift. Mitigation: require warnings and optional strict auditing flags that flip to strict after observed successful conversions

Open question: default behavior for missing required parameters when a default can be derived (e.g., infer from route context). Recommendation: never silently create values; only suggest or coerce when explicit rules exist

Runtime implementation: parsing of x-redwood-call annotations
SDK validation shim to mirror server coercions

Backward-compat tests against historical failing payloads
Performance tests for fuzzy enum matcher and large-schema overhead
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: silent semantic changes leading to user-visible bugs; Mitigation: always record original value and emit warning-level diagnostics, require opt-in for silent coerce without warning
Risk: performance regression in hot path; Mitigation: implement fast-path for common rules and allow per-route toggle
Risk: annotation proliferation causing authoring confusion; Mitigation: ship concise cookbook and linter rules in SDK
